hib_project_model: Project a hibiiscus mixed-effects model

Source: R/hib_project_model.R
hib_project_model.Rd

This function projects a fitted HibModelXXX using the supplied model object and data to be used in projection.

Usage

hib_project_model(
  mod_obj,
  data,
  backtransform = NULL,
  rescale_specs = NULL,
  lme4_specs = NULL,
  inla_specs = NULL,
  brms_specs = NULL,
  calc_aoa = FALSE,
  cv_obj = NULL
)

Arguments

mod_obj

One of; HibModelLME4, HibModelINLA or HibModelBRMS.

data

A data.frame-like object, a SpatRaster, or a list of SpatRaster. Should contain all fixed-effect variables used in the fitted model, and any required random variables. If data is a data.frame, x and y columns should also be included.

backtransform

A function that will backtransform the model response to the scale of the original variable, e.g., exp() as the inverse of log(). Default is NULL, i.e., no backtransformation.

rescale_specs

A named list (or NULL) containing details relevant to rescaling projections. Specifically, named items should consist of:

  • rescale (logical),

  • baseline_covar (data.frame, or NULL),

  • baseline_re_form (formula, NA, or NULL).

In combination, these arguments determine if predictions will be rescaled or not (rescale), the covariate values used to generate the baseline against which other predictions are rescaled (baseline_covar), and whether/how random effects should be incorporated in the generation of this baseline (baseline_re_form, see re_form in lme4/inla/brms_specs argument).
If rescale == TRUE, but no baseline_covar is provided, the intercept of the model will be used as the baseline value.

lme4_specs

A named list (or NULL) containing details relevant to projecting a HibModelLME4.
Named items should consist of:

  • bootstrap (logical), indicating whether bootstrapped prediction intervals should be estimated. Can be slow for large models.

  • n_boot (numeric), how many bootstrap samples should be used to estimate prediction uncertainty.

  • calc_se (logical), specify whether or not a standard error based uncertainty estimate (via marginaleffects::predictions) is calculated and used to generate prediction intervals.

  • conf_level (numeric) is used to specify the confidence levels of intervals generated via bootstrapping or the SE-based approach. Values should fall between 0 and 1, typically in the range 0.5 to 0.95. Multiple values can be provided.

  • re_form (formula, NULL, or NA), as re.form in predict.merMod(), used to specify random effects to condition on when predicting.

inla_specs

A named list (or NULL) containing details relevant to projecting a HibModelINLA.

  • re_form (formula, NULL, or NA), as re.form in predict.merMod(), used to specify random effects to condition on when predicting.

  • link_inverse a function that is the inverse of the link used to fit the model. Used to backtranform the global intercept for use in rescaling predictions.

brms_specs

A named list (or NULL) containing details relevant to projecting a HibModelBRMS. Named items should consist of:

  • incl_obs_uncert (logical), to determine whether or not observation-level uncertainty is included in predictions. Setting this parameter to TRUE will produce predictions using predict.brmsfit() (larger uncertainty), setting to FALSE calls fitted.brmsfit() internally.

  • conf_level (numeric) is used to specify the confidence levels of intervals generated. Values should fall between 0 and 1, typically in the range 0.5 to 0.95. Internally converted to quantiles and passed to the probs argument of predict.brmsfit()/ fitted.brmsfit().

  • re_form (formula, NULL, or NA), as re_formula in predict.brmsfit(), used to specify random effects to condition on when predicting.

calc_aoa

A logical to indicate whether or not the 'Area-of-Applicability' (AOA) should be estimated - following Meyer and Pebesma (2021).

cv_obj

A HibCV object, used in AOA estimation.

Value

HibProjection

Details

Given a HibModelXXX, new data and specification, this function projects/predicts modelled responses for each 'unit' of the new data. Calculation of the 'Area-of-Applicability' of the model within the new data is an optional addition. Specification arguments allow for customisation of the prediction type. If specifications are not provided, defaults will be used. Projections will be returned in the same format as the provided data. If data is provided as SpatRaster, a land-use variable should be included as a single categorical layer, or as multiple, proportional layers, named to align with the levels of the categorical variable. Currently, only a single 'categorical' variable can be provided in 'proportional cover' format in a SpatRaster.

References

  • Meyer, H., & Pebesma, E. (2021). Predicting into unknown space? Estimating the area of applicability of spatial prediction models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 12, 1620–1633. https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13650

  • Meyer H, Milà C, Ludwig M, Linnenbrink J (2023). CAST: 'caret' Applications for Spatial-Temporal Models. R package, https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=CAST.

See also
